title: Enterprise Onboarding, Integration, Escalation & QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates our enterprise onboarding checklist, integration guidance, escalation procedures, and QBR/health-check templates for customers adopting Redwood Inference (Hosted, Dedicated, or Private). It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and SRE teams to run a predictable onboarding and operational lifecycle for enterprise customers.

Key objectives
- Provide a single-source, reproducible onboarding process to reduce time-to-first-value.
- Standardize integration and networking steps to avoid common pitfalls.
- Define clear escalation paths and incident handoffs.
- Supply QBR/health-check templates and metrics to drive renewal conversations.

Audience
- CS Managers and Customer Success Engineers
- Solutions Engineers / Integration Engineers
- Support Engineers and SRE on-call responders

Ownership and SLAs
- Primary owner: customer-success team (Aisha Patel)
- Secondary owner: eng-infra (networking) and eng-serving-runtime (model-serving issues)
- Platform SLOs to reference during onboarding:
  - Hosted API: availability SLO 99.95% (monthly), p95 latency for generation calls < 300ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens).
  - Dedicated: availability SLO 99.9% for reserved capacity, latency targets depend on agreed tier (e.g., p95 < 150ms for low-latency tier).
  - Private (on-prem): responsibility for uptime is shared; Redwood provides installation and day-2 runbooks for configuration and optional support contract for SLAs.

Pre-Onboarding Checklist (SE/CS)
1. Contract and legal sign-offs completed and confidentiality level confirmed.
2. Setup administrative account in Redwood Console; create primary API key and cyclical rotation policy.
3. Identify technical contacts for networking, security, and app owners.
4. Determine deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and expected throughput (tokens/sec, requests/sec).
5. Schedule technical kickoff (60 minutes) with agendas: architecture, security, onboarding milestones.

Technical Kickoff Agenda
- Introductions and roles
- High-level architecture and chosen deployment mode
- Expected traffic profile and SLO targets
- Security requirements: data residency, KMS/HSM, audit log retention
- Network requirements and IP allowlists
- Integration plan and milestones (test plan, canary, rollback)
- QBR cadence and success metrics

Integration Guide (networking, auth, and initial calls)
Networking and Firewall
- Hosted: customers should allow outbound HTTPS to api.redwood.ai and optional egress to our telemetry endpoints for observability.
- Dedicated / Private: provide IP ranges and peering instructions during kickoff. Typical requirements:
  - Ports: 443 (HTTPS), optional 22 for on-prem support access (only when enabled).
  - VPC peering: exchange VPC IDs, CIDR ranges, and configure route tables to allow traffic between customer VPC and Redwood endpoints.
  - DNS: we provide a customer-specific endpoint (e.g., api-customer-123.redwood.internal) for Dedicated/Private.

Authentication and Keys
- API keys are the default auth mechanism for API calls. For Private deployments, support for mTLS or IAM-based auth is available.
- KMS: we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys for Private deployments. Document the key ARN and grant Redwood service principal encrypt/decrypt permissions during onboarding.

Sample cURL to validate API connectivity (Hosted):
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Hello from test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Canary and Traffic Ramp Plan
1. Dry-run: SE runs example requests from customer test environment to verify connectivity and baseline latency.
2. Canary (1-5% of traffic): route a small percentage to Redwood to validate access patterns, responses, and observability hooks.
3. Ramp: increase traffic in staged increments (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with monitoring windows at each step (30-60 minutes) to confirm error rates and latency.
4. Rollback: predefine rollback triggers (error-rate > 2% above baseline for 15 minutes OR p95 latency > 2x target for 10 minutes).

Testing and Validation Checklist
- End-to-end latency and correctness tests with a representative prompt set (record baseline on customer's prior system if available).
- Token-cost and billing validation for sample workloads.
- Functional tests for tool-calling, streaming, and embeddings where used.
- Log and trace correlation (decorate Redwood requests with customer request_id for cross-system tracing).

Escalation Playbook (Support + SRE)
Severity definitions
- P1 (Critical): Complete service outage for customer or severe data integrity issue affecting production. Response target: acknowledge in 15 minutes, initial mitigation within 1 hour.
- P2 (High): Significant degradation (e.g., sustained high error rate, high latency impacting SLA). Response target: acknowledge in 30 minutes, mitigation plan in 4 hours.
- P3 (Medium): Functional bug with workaround or degraded non-critical features. Response target: acknowledge in 1 business day.

Initial Triage (Support)
1. Gather required customer details: customer name, deployment type, region, request IDs, time window, number of affected users, and example request/response (redact PII).
2. Check Redwood Console metrics (error rate, p95 latency) and logs for correlated events.
3. Attempt known-workarounds (see known-issues section). If not resolved, escalate to SRE/Serving Runtime.

Escalation Path and Contacts
- Support Engineer (level 1): support-team@redwood.ai; Slack: #support-queue
- On-call SRE: PagerDuty (refer to customer escalation policy for contact info).
- Serving Runtime senior engineer: ping via Slack @runtime-oncall and +1 via PagerDuty for P1s.
- Customer Success: notify CS immediately for P1/P2 incidents to coordinate customer communications.

Handoff Requirements when Escalating to SRE
- Timestamped logs and request_id scope
- Dashboard snapshots and Grafana links
- Reproduction steps and any attempted mitigations
- Customer impact statement (affected endpoints, feature set)

Communication Templates
- Customer initial acknowledgement (within 30 min): short summary of what we know, immediate next steps, expected update cadence.
- Post-incident summary and RCA: include timeline, root cause, mitigating actions, and planned preventative measures.

Known Issues and Workarounds (examples)
1. Issue ID: RI-2025-089 - Intermittent 500 errors for long-streaming responses
   - Symptoms: streaming sessions terminate with a 500 after ~60s under heavy load.
   - Workaround: reduce per-request max_tokens to 2048 and enable chunked streaming with client-side reassembly.
   - Status: mitigated (hotfix v2025.11), full patch in runtime v2026.02.
2. Issue ID: NET-2026-011 - VPC peering route overlap causing dropped traffic
   - Symptoms: Dedicated customers report failed connections during initial setup.
   - Workaround: confirm non-overlapping CIDRs; if overlap exists, use NAT gateway with proxying or request a dedicated transit gateway setup.
   - Status: guidance documented; SE to assist.
3. Issue ID: AUTH-2026-004 - Token rotation causing short-lived auth failures
   - Symptoms: requests fail with 401 immediately after key rotation.
   - Workaround: use a two-key rotation strategy (create new key, update app, then revoke old key) and stagger rotation times across services.

Known-issues table (copy to customer):
| Issue ID | Symptoms | Workaround | Status | Owner |
| RI-2025-089 | Streaming 500s ~60s | Reduce max_tokens; enable chunked streaming | mitigated | eng-serving-runtime |
| NET-2026-011 | Peering drops | Verify CIDRs; use NAT/proxy | documented | eng-infra |
| AUTH-2026-004 | 401 on rotation | Two-key rotation pattern | recommended | security |

Support Process (day-to-day)
- Tiered support model: Tier-1 (Support Engineers) handle triage and known-workarounds; Tier-2 (SE/SRE) handle deep technical issues and escalations.
- SLA for support responses depends on customer's support tier (Standard/Enterprise). For enterprise: P1 acknowledge < 15 minutes, full incident updates hourly until mitigation.
- Ticket workflow: Zendesk -> Slack #support-queue -> PagerDuty for P1 escalation. Add customer as watcher and CS as a secondary contact in tickets.

Health Checks and QBR Materials
Quarterly Health Check Template
- Metrics to present:
  - Availability (monthly and QTD), error rates by endpoint, p50/p95/p99 latency for core routes
  - Token consumption and cost per 1k tokens (normalized)
  - Throughput: requests/sec and peak concurrency windows
  - Model quality indicators: sample prompt set results, regression alerts triggered
  - Operational items: number of incidents, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to mitigate (MTTM)

QBR Agenda (60-90 min)
1. Executive summary and topline metrics (CS + customer execs)
2. Usage trends and cost analysis (Finance/CS)
3. Reliability and incidents review (SRE)
4. Model performance and quality (Applied ML)
5. Roadmap alignment and upcoming changes (Product)
6. Success plan and next milestones (CS)

QBR Deliverables
- Slide deck with metrics, recommendations, and action items
- Top 3 risks and mitigations for next quarter
- Action log with owners and due dates

Templates and Artifacts
- Sample onboarding timeline (30/60/90 days) checklist
- Canary test scripts and representative prompt-set (attach separately)
- Postmortem template and incident timeline format

Appendix A: 30/60/90 Day Onboarding Checklist (high level)
- Day 0-7: Accounts provisioned, API key rotation policy defined, test connectivity verified
- Day 8-30: Integration tests, canary deployment, performance baseline recorded, cost estimation validated
- Day 31-90: Full traffic ramp, QBR scheduling, automation of alerts and tracing, runbooks handed over to customer ops

Appendix B: Quick Reference Commands
- Verify connectivity (curl): see example above.
- Fetch account usage (CLI example):
redwoodctl usage get --account-id acct_123 --start 2026-07-01 --end 2026-07-31

Appendix C: Escalation RACI
- Support: Responsible for triage and communication
- SE: Responsible for integration issues and configuration fixes
- SRE: Responsible for runtime incidents and mitigation
- CS: Account communication and escalation to customer
- Product: Decisions about large-scope behavioral changes or product bugs
